- Clarify license geography and whether the license grant permits deployments in our contracted sites (US-only, but some data centers in the future may be in Canada).
- Define what constitutes a permissible "Operator" for witness access and whether we can insist on a third‑party witness during snapshot handover.
- Audit evidence: we need a concrete list of artifacts Redwood will provide (forensic snapshot, logs, attestation report). Do you offer a sealed snapshot/escrow pathway?
- KMS/HSM custody questions: do you require us to use customer-managed keys for on‑prem, or is Redwood's KMS acceptable?

We are aiming to sign the order by end of month but need these clarifications next week. Can we set a short call with your legal/ops leads?

Hi Danielle —

Appreciate the clear redlines and timeline. Looping in Laura (legal), Rishi (ops/privdeploy lead) and Vanessa (solutions/ordering) so we can respond with concrete language and an evidence matrix. Quick answers up front:

- Territory: Redwood's standard MSA grants a worldwide license with territory carveouts configurable on the order form. For your case we can add an explicit "Restricted Territory: United States and Canada" clause and mirror that in the order form exhibits.

- Operator / Witness: We can support both: (1) live third‑party witness during a sealed snapshot handover; or (2) a remote attestation package plus a notarized log bundle. Live witnessing requires a short witness window and a signed acknowledgement (exhibit).

- Evidence artifacts: Rishi will propose a minimal evidence set (forensic snapshot hash, access logs for witness session, attestation report, and downloadable sanitized runbook). We also have an "escrow-lite" path used for regulated customers — snapshot + checksum deposit with time-bound witness.

- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) for private deployments; Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable for hosted/dedicated but not for on‑prem legal-required custody scenarios. If you require HSM-backed key custody, we will add the requirement to the order form and a short exhibit describing key handover.

Can we schedule a 30‑minute sync Tuesday or Wednesday PST? Rishi — can you take point on the evidence matrix and attach Redwood's draft addendum? Laura — note we'll likely need two redline passes: one for legal text (license/indemnity/scope) and one operational (witness windows, orderform exhibits).

Thanks — talk soon.

Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA & Order Form redlines (on-prem scope + audit evidence)

Tessa / Rishi —

Reviewing the customer redlines and Redwood's draft addendum. My high‑level recommendations to keep negotiations tight and auditable:

1) License Geography: Add an "Exhibit A: Deployment Territory" to the Order Form. Language: "Customer may deploy and operate the licensed software at Customer-controlled sites within the territories expressly listed in Exhibit A. Any additional territories require written amendment to the Order Form."

2) Operator Definition: Replace broad "Operator" language with: "Operator(s) means individuals expressly designated by Customer in writing prior to any witness session; Operator credentials and roles must be mutually agreed 10 business days prior to the session." This prevents ambiguous external vendor claims.

3) Witnessing and Snapshot: Two discrete options in the exhibit — (a) Sealed Snapshot Handover (in-person or approved third‑party witness) — Redwood provides sealed snapshot, hash, and access log coverage for the witnessing window; or (b) Remote Attestation Package — attestation signed by Redwood's CTO + logs + runbook excerpt. Operational requirements/timelines should be appended as a table (witness window length, notice period, retention).

4) Evidence & Retention: Provide a short artifacts matrix (Artifact | Provided by | Retention period | Format). Recommend default retention 90 days for witness artifacts unless otherwise agreed.

5) KMS/HSM: Add an optional order form exhibit titled "Key Custody" with two selectable boxes: "Customer-managed KMS (required)" or "Redwood-managed KMS (acceptable)". If customer selects BYO KMS, include a minimal integration SLA for key rotation and handback.

6) Signature / Escrow-lite: For speed, propose an "escrow-lite" statement: an independent checksum deposit with time-stamped notarization (no full code escrow). This is often acceptable to procurement and avoids heavy legal processes.

I'll prepare a redline doc with the specific patch language for the MSA sections: License Grant (Sec 2), Definitions (Operators), and Order Form Exhibits. Rishi — please add the artifacts matrix and witness logistics to the addendum draft.

Laura Bennett
Deputy General Counsel
Redwood Inference
